title: English Muffins
subtitle: soft, nook-filled rounds cooked on the stovetop
excerpt: English muffins are cooked in a dry frying pan, not the oven. This gives them their pale, floury exterior and the characteristic nooks inside when you fork-split them. They are the right vessel for eggs Benedict and the best vehicle for melted butter.
sourceNotes: Traditional British bakery staple, now associated worldwide with breakfast and brunch.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze split. Toast directly from frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape, dust in semolina, and refrigerate overnight on a tray. Cook cold from the fridge.
recipe.temperatureNote: Stovetop -- low to medium heat in a dry cast iron or heavy frying pan

content.text: Cook English muffins over a low heat. They need 6 to 8 minutes each side. If the pan is too hot the outside will colour before the inside has cooked through. Patience is the technique here -- low and slow gives you the spring and the right interior texture.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with the sugar. Leave 5 minutes. Combine flour and salt. Add the milk mixture and melted butter. Mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Place in a greased bowl, cover, and prove for 1 hour until doubled.
Dust the worktop with semolina or plain flour. Roll the dough to about 2cm thick. Cut into rounds with a 9cm cutter. Place on a floured tray, dust the tops, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan or cast iron skillet over a low to medium heat. Do not oil it. Cook the muffins in batches for 6 to 8 minutes per side until cooked through and lightly coloured.
Cool on a rack. To split, pierce the edge with a fork all the way around and prise apart. Never cut with a knife -- it compresses the interior and kills the nooks.

items.symptom: Muffins are doughy in the middle
items.cause: Pan was too hot and the outsides browned before the inside cooked through.
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium-low throughout. If in doubt, test one first and adjust.

items.cause: Cut with a knife instead of forked apart.
items.fix: Use a fork. Pierce the circumference all the way around, then twist. The open holes in the interior will be revealed.

content.text: Despite the name, English muffins as we know them are partly an American phenomenon -- the griddle-cooked round became a US diner staple and found fame in eggs Benedict. In Britain they were always griddle breads, baked in bakeries on heavy iron plates. They remain a standard item in British supermarkets and a weekend breakfast classic.
